latestRelease.notes:
# Agent

### Prelude

Released on: 2026-08-11

- Please refer to the [7.82.1 tag on integrations-core](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/blob/master/AGENT_CHANGELOG.md#datadog-agent-version-7821) for the list of changes on the Core Checks

### Bug Fixes

- Windows: Fixed an issue where an explicit `DDAGENTUSER_KEEP_RIGHTS` or `DDAGENTUSER_NAME` value passed as an install argument to a Fleet Automation-triggered Windows Agent install/upgrade could be silently overridden by a stale fallback value (respectively from the registry and from the running service account).
- Fix an issue where GPU monitoring could trigger a kernel panic on multi-GPU nodes with Hopper/Blackwell GPUs.

signals.title: [TEEP-4881] feat(logs): add metric for messages discarded during file rotation
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds observability for messages discarded during file rotation when `close_timeout` expires: - New `logs.messages_discarded_context_cancelled` telemetry metric - New `MessagesDiscarded` expvar counter - Warning log when messages are discarded with guidance to increase `DD_LOGS_CONFIG_CLOSE_TIMEOUT` ### Motivation In `pkg/logs/tailers/file/tailer.go:424-428`, when the forward context is cancelled (e.g., during rotation timeout), in-flight messages are silently discarded with no telemetry. Users cannot distinguish between "logs were read but discarded" and "logs were never read." This makes it difficult for users with slow pipelines to tune `close_timeout` appropriately since they have no visibility into whether messages are being lost. ### Describe how you validated your changes 1. **Unit test**: Added `TestMessagesDiscardedMetric` that verifies the metric is incremented when messages are discarded due to context cancellation 2. **Manual testing**: Built a debug agent with temporary logging at the discard code path, deployed to EC2, and confirmed the discard triggers during file rotation with a blocked pipeline 3. **Existing tests**: All existing tests in `pkg/logs/metrics` and `pkg/logs/tailers/file` pass ### Additional Notes - This is a low-risk observability enhancement - no changes to existing behavior - The metric name `messages_discarded_context_cancelled` clearly indicates the cause - The warning log includes the `close_timeout` value and suggests increasing `DD_LOGS_CONFIG_CLOSE_TIMEOUT`
signals.author: ArmentaRoberto

signals.title: [PROF-13750] Handle proxy/FIPS/custom URLs in host-profiler converter endpoint inference
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Fixes endpoint inference in the host-profiler converter when `apm_config.profiling_dd_url` or `profiling_additional_endpoints` points to a proxy, FIPS localhost, or other non-Datadog URL. After #46356, `ExtractSiteFromURL` returns empty for any hostname not in the known Datadog domain list. In `newConfigManager` this caused those endpoints to be skipped entirely, leaving inferred OTLP exporters and symbol endpoints empty and stopping profile/symbol delivery. **Changes in `converter_with_agent.go`:** 1. `newConfigManager`: preserve endpoints with empty site when a valid URL is present (previously skipped) 2. `inferOtlpHTTPConfig`: when site is empty, build profiles endpoint as URL + path using `extractBaseURL`; skip metrics with warning 3. `inferHostProfilerEndpointConfig`: when site is empty, skip symbol endpoint inference with warning; disable symbol uploader when no Datadog endpoints available 4. FIPS localhost URLs follow the same proxy path (Info log, not Warn) ### Motivation Users with proxy or FIPS configurations get broken profile/symbol delivery because `ExtractSiteFromURL` returns empty for non-Datadog hostnames, and the converter skips those endpoints entirely. ### Describe how you validated your changes - 3 new golden-file test cases in `TestConverterWithAgentProxyURL`: `proxy_profiling_dd_url`, `fips_localhost_url`, `proxy_additional_endpoint` - Full converter test suite passes with no regressions - Existing Datadog URL tests (`TestConverterWithAgent`, `TestConverterWithAgentDCSite`) still pass ### Additional Notes - **Draft**: Deferring actual implementation until the host-profiler moves from a converter to a confmap provider with a dedicated `datadog.yaml` key for profiler config. This PR serves as a reference implementation. - Jira: PROF-13750 - Depends on: #46356

signals.title: [DO NOT MERGE] One-off e2e run with ADP enabled by default
signals.text: ## Summary Temporarily flips \`data_plane.enabled\` from \`false\` to \`true\` in the agent's compiled-in config default so that every e2e test in the full suite runs against ADP without requiring per-test changes or test duplication. The change is throwaway — close without merging once the CI run completes. This is the same config knob used by the AMP ADP test helpers (DADP-72, see [Slack thread](https://dd.slack.com/archives/C070PQKLLP5/p1783453441368899)). ## How to kick off the full e2e suite Trigger a new pipeline on this branch and set the CI variable: \`\`\` RUN_E2E_TESTS=on \`\`\` That variable hits the \`if_run_all_e2e_tests\` rule in \`.gitlab-ci.yml\` and flips all e2e jobs from manual to \`on_success\`. ## CI findings (ADP 1.5.1, branch jszwedko/run-ci-adp-enabled) ### Fixed in this PR - **Windows MSI \`status_command_infos\`**: All MSI test variants fail because \`agent_behaviour.go\` asserts the status output contains "DogStatsD". When ADP handles DSD, the \`DogStatsD\` status section is absent (the \`EnabledInternal()\` guard prevents registering the status provider). Fixed by accepting either "DogStatsD" or "Dogstatsd Metric Sample" (always present in the Aggregator section). ### Known pre-existing failures (ADP limitations, tracked in Saluki) - **\`TestReplayWithTagEnrichment\`** — ADP doesn't enrich replayed DSD packets with current tagger state. Tracked in Saluki. ### New failures requiring Saluki fixes - **Container DSD tests (ECS \`TestDogtstatsdUDP\`, \`TestDogtstatsdUDS\`; Kind \`dogstatsd-uds\` pods)**: In container environments (ECS, K8s/Kind), fakeintake is configured as \`DD_ADDITIONAL_ENDPOINTS\` rather than \`dd_url\`. ADP doesn't appear to forward DogStatsD metrics to \`additional_endpoints\`, so no metrics arrive at fakeintake. In VM tests where fakeintake IS \`dd_url\` (primary endpoint), DSD forwarding works. This points to an \`additional_endpoints\` forwarding gap in ADP. - The Kind \`dogstatsd-uds\` pods fail to become Ready — the workload pods mount \`/var/run/datadog/dsd.socket\` as a HostPath volume (type \`Socket\`). With ADP enabled, the core agent's DSD server doesn't start (so no socket is created); ADP must create it but apparently doesn't complete socket setup in time or at the expected path. - Root cause: ADP \`additional_endpoints\` forwarding — active Saluki config migration work (issues #2312–#2316) may be the upstream cause. ### Other failures under investigation - **Anomaly detection tests** — under investigation, may be ADP-independent - **GPU tests** — under investigation ## Test plan - No new tests. The goal is to observe which existing e2e tests break when ADP is the default. - \`new-e2e-amp-adp\` (existing) runs the AMP suite filtered to \`--run "ADP"\` tests; this PR covers the rest. **DO NOT MERGE** — this default flip must not land on \`main\`.

Check the [Dependency Dashboard](../issues/33469) for more information. --- ### dd-trace-go: Improper parsing of W3C baggage headers may lead to DoS [CVE-2026-50274](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-50274) / [GHSA-74j5-xf3v-crq8](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-74j5-xf3v-crq8) <details> <summary>More information</summary> #### Details ##### Impact Datadog tracing libraries that implement W3C baggage propagation parse incoming baggage HTTP headers without enforcing item-count or byte-size limits on the extract path. The DD_TRACE_BAGGAGE_MAX_ITEMS (default 64) and DD_TRACE_BAGGAGE_MAX_BYTES (default 8192) limits were applied only to baggage injection, not extraction. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can send a request whose baggage header contains an arbitrarily large number of comma-separated key-value pairs (or a single very large value). The tracer allocates a hash-map entry for each pair on every request, causing unbounded CPU and memory consumption and enabling a remote Denial of Service against any HTTP service that has the baggage propagation style enabled. The baggage propagation style is enabled by default in most affected tracers, so any internet-facing service that has been instrumented with an affected tracer version is exposed unless the propagation style has been explicitly narrowed. ##### Patches This is resolved in version 2.8.1 and later of the `dd-trace-go` library. ##### Workarounds If users cannot upgrade immediately: 1. OTel process context v2 (OTLP proto format) is supported ([#​4478](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4478)), and the `parentbased_always_on` sampler works in OTLP mode ([#​4567](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4567)). **Large Language Model (LLM) Observability.** Prompt tracking is now available for LLMObs spans ([#​4608](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4608)). Experiment scope propagates from APM baggage into spans automatically ([#​4651](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4651)). **Profiler.** An experimental goroutine leak profile is available as opt-in ([#​4420](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4420)). The goroutine wait profile type has been removed — this is a breaking change for anyone using it explicitly ([#​4589](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4589)). **HTTP and tracing.** A new environment variable `DD_TRACE_HTTP_URL_QUERY_STRING_ALLOWLIST` lets you whitelist query string parameters to keep unredacted ([#​4562](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4562)). A new `tracer.StartSpanFromPropagatedContext` API simplifies span creation from propagated contexts ([#​4492](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4492)). AWS EventBridge max payload size is bumped to 1 MB ([#​4458](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4458)). Envoy Service Extensions integration gains Unix Domain Socket (UDS) support ([#​4463](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4463)). **OpenFeature.** Flag evaluation metrics now emit via OTel Metrics ([#​4489](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4489)), with allocation key tagging ([#​4515](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4515)) and Remote Configuration (RC) integration via `FFE_FLAGS` subscription at tracer startup ([#​4495](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4495)). **Bug fixes.** gorm now respects `DD_TRACE_REMOVE_INTEGRATION_SERVICE_NAMES_ENABLED` ([#​4618](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4618)). Redis and Valkey pipeline commands are joined with newlines, fixing agent obfuscation ([#​4593](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4593)). A race condition in HTTP client trace timings is resolved ([#​4591](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4591)). AppSec block responses now include a correct `Content-Length` header ([#​4496](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4496)), and spurious Remote Configuration errors are silenced when RC is disabled ([#​4612](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4612)). `ContextWithSpan` no longer panics on nil context ([#​4313](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4313)). The OTel bridge preserves keep/drop sampling decisions for unsampled spans ([#​4631](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4631)). User-provided DogStatsD addresses now correctly take priority over defaults ([#​4575](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4575)). **Performance.** Trace ID hex encoding is cached ([#​4481](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4481)), the span metadata map is preallocated ([#​4541](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4541)), and locking is removed from both sampling priority access ([#​4546](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4546)) and the internal logger ([#​4547](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4547)) — reducing allocations and contention on hot paths. **CI Visibility.** Bazel offline cache and payload-file modes are supported ([#​4503](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4503)). signals.title: [ABLD-461] [ABLD-528] Switch some of pkg/ network and ebpf to select() rather than relying only on tags.
signals.text: [ABLD-461] Switch some of pkg/ network and ebpf to select() rather than relying only on tags. ### What does this PR do? - remove `target_compatible_with = [linux]` on //pkg/epbf. This means a lot of test targets which were silently skipped on other platforms now try to build. - Switch some network and bpf code to hand build select() clauses. - This allows us to make the dependencies match what is actually needed based on the sources which get complied for each tag. - it makes it explicit that ebpf is only used on linux - converts //pkg/network/... to dd_agent_go_test because now that we are trying those tests, we actually need the gotags. - The important outcome: This allows agent to build for macos!!! ### Motivation This unblocks building the agent on all platforms which is a high priority goal, as that unblocks the rest of Q3 work on packaging and security. The alternative is to find and remove every target_compatible_with=linux setting on a transitive dependent of //cmd/agent:agent. To do that - we would have to change every test which might depend on this from go_test to dd_agent_go_test - and probably figure out which ones need explicit linux_bpf tags added, but this adds a new config, wasting CI time - and it is less efficient than just having a smaller build graph. ### Describe how you validated your changes Build and run it on macos. ``` $ bazel run //cmd/agent:agent -- version ... Target //cmd/agent:agent up-to-date: bazel-bin/cmd/agent/agent_/agent INFO: Elapsed time: 7.941s, Critical Path: 7.17s INFO: Running command line: bazel-bin/cmd/agent/agent_/agent <args omitted> Agent 7.83.0-localbuild - Commit: dev - Serialization version: v5.0.205 - Go version: go1.26.5 ``` ### Additional Notes We should remove `--skip_incompatible_explicit_targets` from the global bazelrc. It allowed us to accumulate tech debt by making things that *appeared* to be sound but were silently just not building. Now that we are at the end of the migration, we need to surface the unfinished work. signals.title: fix(devcontainer): don't remap UID on macOS
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Stops the dev container from realigning its `dd` user to the host UID on macOS. `tasks/devcontainer.py` now passes `HOST_UID`/`HOST_GID` **only on Linux**, and sets `updateRemoteUserUID: false`. ### Motivation On macOS the Docker VM's file sharing (virtiofs on Colima/OrbStack, gRPC-FUSE/virtiofs on Docker Desktop) already maps container writes back to the host user regardless of the container UID, so the realignment is unnecessary. Worse, the dev-env image entrypoint's `usermod -u dd` races the dev container CLI's `docker exec -u dd` (onCreateCommand) and aborts the container: ``` usermod: user dd is currently used by process N -> exit 137 ``` Docker Desktop happened to win that race; Colima's `docker exec` timing loses it, so startup fails reliably there — which matters now that engineering is migrating off Docker Desktop to Colima. On native-Linux hosts the IDs are still passed, since bind mounts there preserve the host UID and the realignment is genuinely required. ### Describe how you validated your changes Full `dda inv devcontainer.start` (`devcontainer up` → entrypoint + `install-tools` + `deps`, 191 modules) → `{"outcome":"success"}` on macOS (Apple Silicon) / Colima `vz`+`virtiofs`. ### ⚠️ Also required for macOS: the dev-env image fix This PR is independently correct, but macOS/Colima startup hits a **second, independent** crash: the image entrypoint's `chown -R` of the home dir dies on a unix socket in a bind-mounted `~/.ssh` over virtiofs. That is fixed in **DataDog/datadog-agent-buildimages#1292**, which requires the `datadog/agent-dev-env-linux` image to be **rebuilt and rolled out**. Both this PR and that image bump are needed for macOS to be fully green. ### Possible Drawbacks / Trade-offs None on Linux (behavior unchanged). On macOS/Windows the image-side UID realignment no longer runs, which is the intended fix. ### Release note Dev-tooling change under `tasks/`, no user-facing impact — `changelog/no-changelog`.

signals.title: [ACTP] [PAR split deployment] shut down idle private action executor
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds a self-termination watchdog to the on-demand Go executor. Dispatch activity resets the idle timer; health checks do not, and active actions suppress idle shutdown. The watchdog uses three times `private_action_runner.idle_timeout_seconds` (60 seconds by default) so `par-control` remains the primary owner of idle shutdown. It applies only to executor mode; the monolithic runner is unchanged. ### Validation - `bazel test //pkg/privateactionrunner/executor:executor_test` - `bazel test //comp/privateactionrunner/impl:impl_test` - `bazel test //cmd/privateactionrunner/subcommands/runexecutor:runexecutor_test` _Stack 1 of 9; followed by #54589._

This preserves the license we were using before. It also preserves the fact that the Omnibus build was using a personal copy cached at https://dd-agent-omnibus.s3.amazonaws.com/licenses/Python-2.0. That's not great - we should use the upstream license, but the upstream license is not a true copy of the license. It has history which is unrelated to the current license, so it is actually less good than our copy. This is a thing to sort out in the future. signals.title: feat(softinv): report the OS and OEM kernel-mode drivers
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Extends the software inventory beyond installed applications with two new software types, `os` and `driver`: | Platform | Type | Source | |---|---|---| | Windows | `driver` | `Win32_SystemDriver`, plus `Win32_PnPSignedDriver` joined against `Win32_PnPEntity` | | Windows | `os` | `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion` | | macOS | `os` | `/System/Library/CoreServices/SystemVersion.plist` | **Operating system.** One entry whose version advances, rather than one entry per update. An update is an event, not an installed item whose version moves, so it would produce a permanently static entry — and the host SBOM already carries installed KBs. Name and product code are constant, because the backend keys an item on name + product code with the version excluded; anything version-derived in either field would make an upgrade read as remove + install. The version carries the full patch level: `10.0.26100.4652` on Windows including the UBR, `15.6 (24G84)` on macOS including the build that supplemental updates and RSRs advance. **Drivers.** Only OEM and third-party drivers are reported; the drivers that ship with Windows are excluded. Two sources, because each sees what the other cannot. `Win32_SystemDriver` covers drivers registered as kernel services, including software-only ones — EDR minifilters, network and DLP filters — that have no PnP device node. The class carries no version or vendor, so both come from the version resource of the image path; only the numeric `VS_FIXEDFILEINFO` version is accepted, since the `FileVersion` string is routinely decorated or comma-separated. Image paths are normalized (`\??\`, `\SystemRoot\`, `%SystemRoot%`, relative) and MUI display names (`@<dll>,-<id>`) resolved with `SHLoadIndirectString`. Filtered on the binary's `CompanyName`, the only vendor signal the class offers; an absent `CompanyName` is kept, since an unattributed kernel driver is worth seeing. Identity is the service name, which Windows guarantees unique. `Win32_PnPSignedDriver` covers packages bound to a device that register no kernel service of their own, which the first source cannot see. Selected by the INF being published as `oemNN.inf` — `Manufacturer` is not used, because Microsoft's inbox INFs report generic strings such as `(Standard system devices)` and Windows also ships inbox INFs authored by hardware vendors, so filtering on it would keep hundreds of inbox drivers. One `Win32_PnPEntity` query is joined in memory to skip devices that already have a service; a query per device would spend the entire time budget on the join. Identity is the device name, the field the class offers that survives a driver update. Known limitations: UMDF user-mode drivers register no kernel service, and a driver whose service entry is created, loaded, then deleted is invisible. This is an inventory of registered drivers, not of code currently in the kernel. **Deadline.** Each collector is bounded at 90s in the shared snapshot runner. A timeout is fatal, because a timed-out enumeration is an unknown state and a missing row reads downstream as a removal; zero rows is still a valid result. A hung native call cannot be cancelled — the WMI library takes no context — so a collector that misses its deadline is not started again until it returns. ### Motivation The inventory only covered installed applications, leaving OS patch level and kernel drivers invisible — two of the most useful signals for fleet visibility and compliance. The deadline is a prerequisite rather than a nicety: these sources can block, and a single slow `Collect()` previously stalled the whole snapshot with no upper bound. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Windows unit tests run and pass in CI (`tests_windows-x64`); macOS unit tests pass locally; `bazel test //pkg/inventory/software:software_test` passes. - `dda inv linter.go` clean, and clean again under `GOOS=windows`, which type-checks the Windows-tagged files and their tests. - Coverage: deadline and in-flight behaviour, both driver filters, the PnP/service join including case mismatch and devices missing from `Win32_PnPEntity`, path normalization and MUI resolution, the numeric-version requirement, identity stability across a version bump for both driver sources, and entry-ID uniqueness once the new families merge with application entries. - Real-host integration tests compare collected drivers against the `Services` registry key, assert nothing Microsoft-published survives the service filter, and log the OEM/inbox split per source; the macOS one asserts the running version against `sw_vers -productVersion`. - Driver payloads from a real Windows host were inspected end to end. That caught two drivers reporting an unresolved MUI reference as their name, fixed in 2741b66. ### Additional Notes - A fatal error from any single collector still drops the whole snapshot (existing behaviour). - PnP-sourced entries carry no `install_paths`, because `Win32_PnPSignedDriver` names no binary. - Enable with `software_inventory.enabled: true`, which drives both the system-probe module and the core agent component. No status or flare changes were needed, since `populateStatus` already groups by `Source`. - Worst-case snapshot duration is bounded per collector, not globally, so it scales with collector count. A snapshot-wide ceiling would be a separate change.

signals.title: feat(otel-metrics): share SDK trace stats mapping
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds a transport-neutral `sdktracestats` package under `opentelemetry-mapping-go`. `BuildSDKTraceStatsPayload` owns SDK metric recognition, field mapping, validation, normalized tags, time windows, per-datapoint error isolation, and lossless sparse-histogram construction. The caller supplies envelope metadata such as source and hostname. The package returns shared APM-stats fields without depending on the Agent or dd-source protobuf types. ### Motivation The Agent and public OTLP metrics intake need to convert `traces.span.sdk.metrics.duration` into the same APM trace-stats contract. Keeping two mappings would let tags, status handling, histogram validation, and operation naming drift. This PR makes one mapping implementation the source of truth while leaving transport adapters and delivery local to each consumer. ### Stack and shipping order 1. This PR merges first as the shared code dependency. 2. [ddoghq/dd-source#56526](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/56526) and [DataDog/datadog-agent#53167](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53167) then consume it and can be reviewed in parallel. 3. signals.title: [SVLS-9526] Prototype: serverless-init inventory payload + 9-platform POC deploy scripts
signals.text: ## What this is A **prototype branch** containing the full stack of changes for SVLS-9526 in a single PR. Intended for review and discussion — these changes will be broken into the stacked PRs below before merge. ## Stacked PRs (final form) | PR | Branch | Contents | |---|---|---| | #54537 | `svls-9526/force-collect` | `ForceCollect()` — send inventory payload on every cold start | | #54538 | `svls-9526/diagnostic-v2` | `inventories_first_run_delay` config key + diagnostic enhancements | | #54543 | `svls-9526/serverless-agent-table` | `cmd/serverless-init/inventory`: `serverless_*` fields in inventoryagent payload | ## What's in this PR **Agent changes (will land via the stacked PRs above):** - `ForceCollect()` added to `inventoryagent.Component` — fires before `modeConf.Runner()` so the inventory payload is sent before the container can scale to zero - `inventories_first_run_delay` config key to control startup delay - New `cmd/serverless-init/inventory` package: populates `serverless_*` fields (cloud provider, workload type, origin, resource name, deployment model, runtime, agent commit, DD config) into the inventoryagent payload - Enhanced startup diagnostics (`DD_SERVERLESS_DIAGNOSTIC_INFO=true`) including UUID, CCRID, and inventory pipeline config **POC deploy scripts (`scripts/serverless-deploy/`, not intended to merge to main):** - Deploys 9 test services across GCP (Cloud Run Service/Job/Function) and Azure (Container App, Web App Containers, Web App SITECONTAINERS, Web App Linux Code) - `demo.sh` — one-command end-to-end runner: build → deploy all 9 → trigger cold starts → collect logs → print REDAPL SQL query ## How to run the POC ```bash export GCP_PROJECT=datadog-serverless-gcp-demo export AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID=<sub-id> export DD_API_KEY=$(vault kv get -field=api_key kv/dd/api_keys/dddev) export IMAGE_TAG=1.10.2-poc-$(date +%Y%m%d) cd scripts/serverless-deploy ./demo.sh ``` ###dd-auth command equivalent: `export DD_API_KEY=$(dd-auth vault kv get -field=api_key kv/dd/api_keys/dddev)` Or if it's wrapping the whole script: `dd-auth ./demo.sh ` Then paste the generated SQL into **go/redapl → Queries → SQL** to see the agents in `datadog_agent`. ## Key findings from 9-platform testing | Platform | UUID behaviour | `datadog_agent` rows | |---|---|---| | GCP Cloud Run | New UUID per cold start | `ForceCollect()` required — container scales to zero before 60s delay | | Azure Container App | Stable UUID per replica | Upserts same row reliably | | Azure Web App | DMI UUID from underlying VM | Apps on same App Service Plan share UUID → need CCRID-based PK | This motivates `serverless_init_agent` (SVLS-9604): a separate REDAPL table keyed by `resource_id` (CCRID) instead of Agent UUID. ## Not in scope for merge - `scripts/serverless-deploy/` — test infrastructure only, not shipped in the agent - `scripts/serverless-deploy/diagnostic-results-*.txt` — personal test output

signals.title: Skip full git clones on Windows package jobs
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Stop Windows MSI/zip package jobs from doing a full git clone (`GIT_DEPTH: 0`). They only needed history so `get_version()` could run `git describe --tags` inside the build container, which has no AWS credentials. Instead, download `agent-version.cache` on the runner host (after `assume-role`) and fail the job if that copy fails. The file is mounted into the container and xcopied into the buildroot, so `get_version()` reads the cache and never calls `git describe`. ### Motivation Full clones of this repo are expensive. These jobs can use the pipeline-default shallow clone once versioning comes from `setup_agent_version`'s S3 cache. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Confirmed `go_deps` already `needs: setup_agent_version`, so the cache object exists before package jobs start. - Confirmed the host `before_script` `assume-role` still runs (this change is in `script`, so it is not overwritten). - S3 copy uses the same `Invoke-Expression` + `$lastExitCode` pattern as `.upload_sbom_artifacts_windows`, because PowerShell 5 does not fail the job on a native `aws.exe` error. ### Additional Notes CI-only; no release note. Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

signals.title: Add baseline Dynamic Tests for Cloud Network Monitoring
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Adds an opt-in baseline profile for Cloud Network Monitoring Dynamic Tests. When `network_path.connections_monitoring.baseline_tests_enabled` is enabled and CNM is effectively running, the Agent: - retains bounded approximate top sets for diagnostic and healthy connections; - selects up to three priority connections per fixed 30-minute window; - schedules selected paths through the normal recurring path-test lifecycle; - bypasses mutable Remote Configuration filters for baseline eligibility; - reports the `baseline` dynamic-test profile in Network Path payloads and telemetry. Explicit recurring Dynamic Tests continue to take precedence and use the `standard` profile. NetFlow behavior remains independent. When the baseline setting is false, it does not enable the collector or baseline machinery. ### Motivation Provide a small included set of representative CNM path tests without retaining every observed connection or flow. The selector is capped at 128 diagnostic and 128 healthy candidates and uses the existing `xxhash` dependency to keep memory and allocation overhead low. Implementation follows: - [RFC: Baseline Dynamic Tests for CNM](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/NP2/pages/7091453953/RFC+Baseline+Dynamic+Tests+for+CNM) - [Implementation Contract](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/NP2/pages/7091486978/Baseline+Dynamic+Tests+for+CNM+-+Implementation+Contract) ### Describe how you validated your changes - Focused Bazel builds and unit tests for collector state, selection, windowing, filtering, recurring baseline store behavior, payloads, configuration, rDNS, and traceroute activation. - Bazel race tests for the collector and path-test store. - Configuration schema lint. - [AI] The existing Network Path dynamic-tests E2E now includes a baseline-only packaged Agent suite that drives real host CNM traffic and asserts the fakeintake payload profile, traceroute, and baseline execution telemetry. - The E2E binary builds locally and exposes both standard and baseline suite entry points; cloud execution uses the existing `new-e2e-netpath` CI job. - A high-cardinality benchmark over 65,536 unique connections retained exactly 128 candidates with approximately 42 KB allocated across 134 allocations. - Tests verify exact-heavy-hitter recovery, deterministic ties, saturation, downstream channel pressure, Remote Configuration isolation, disabled-state behavior, and recurring TTL-boundary compatibility. ### Additional Notes The baseline enablement setting is intentionally internal during rollout: it remains in the configuration schema for validation, but has no `visibility: public` marker and is deliberately omitted from the generated `datadog.yaml` examples. The baseline selection window is intentionally fixed at 30 minutes and does not inherit `network_path.collector.pathtest_interval`. It controls selection only, not path-test lifetime: a newly selected path runs immediately and then at the normal `pathtest_interval` until normal TTL expiry. Reselecting a live path refreshes its TTL without resetting its existing cadence, and paths may therefore continue running beyond the window in which they were selected.

signal.title: remove unneeded python spec in legacy omnibus
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Remove unneeded python spec in legcay omnibus - Lift python3.rb dependency up datadog-agent-integrations-py3 - Add the missing license declaration for //deps:cpython - put all the files for cpython together in deps/cpython. This preserves the license we were using before. It also preserves the fact that the Omnibus build was using a personal copy cached at https://dd-agent-omnibus.s3.amazonaws.com/licenses/Python-2.0. That's not great - we should use the upstream license, but the upstream license is not a true copy of the license. It has history which is unrelated to the current license, so it is actually less good than our copy. This is a thing to sort out in the future. At least now the fact that we use a private copy is explicit, rather than being hidden in the omnibus code. ### Motivation - Do not specify the python version in two places but only use it in one. - Remove dead code ### Describe how you validated your changes - CI - Missing file detector does not show that we lost the license. Early runs did, so I have confidence that CI correctly detects it.

signal.title: Add baseline Dynamic Tests for Cloud Network Monitoring
signal.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Adds an opt-in baseline profile for Cloud Network Monitoring Dynamic Tests. When `network_path.connections_monitoring.baseline_tests_enabled` is enabled and CNM is effectively running, the Agent: - retains bounded approximate top sets for diagnostic and healthy connections; - selects up to three priority connections per fixed 30-minute window; - schedules selected paths through the normal recurring path-test lifecycle; - bypasses mutable Remote Configuration filters for baseline eligibility; - reports the `baseline` dynamic-test profile in Network Path payloads and telemetry. Explicit recurring Dynamic Tests continue to take precedence and use the `standard` profile. NetFlow behavior remains independent. When the baseline setting is false, it does not enable the collector or baseline machinery. ### Motivation Provide a small included set of representative CNM path tests without retaining every observed connection or flow. The selector is capped at 128 diagnostic and 128 healthy candidates and uses the existing `xxhash` dependency to keep memory and allocation overhead low. Implementation follows: - [RFC: Baseline Dynamic Tests for CNM](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/NP2/pages/7091453953/RFC+Baseline+Dynamic+Tests+for+CNM) - [Implementation Contract](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/NP2/pages/7091486978/Baseline+Dynamic+Tests+for+CNM+-+Implementation+Contract) ### Describe how you validated your changes - Focused Bazel builds and unit tests for collector state, selection, windowing, filtering, recurring baseline store behavior, payloads, configuration, rDNS, and traceroute activation. - Bazel race tests for the collector and path-test store. - Configuration schema lint. - [AI] The existing Network Path dynamic-tests E2E now includes a baseline-only packaged Agent suite that drives real host CNM traffic and asserts the fakeintake payload profile, traceroute, and baseline execution telemetry. - The E2E binary builds locally and exposes both standard and baseline suite entry points; cloud execution uses the existing `new-e2e-netpath` CI job. - A high-cardinality benchmark over 65,536 unique connections retained exactly 128 candidates with approximately 42 KB allocated across 134 allocations. - Tests verify exact-heavy-hitter recovery, deterministic ties, saturation, downstream channel pressure, Remote Configuration isolation, disabled-state behavior, and recurring TTL-boundary compatibility. ### Additional Notes The baseline enablement setting is intentionally internal during rollout: it remains in the configuration schema for validation, but has no `visibility: public` marker and is deliberately omitted from the generated `datadog.yaml` examples. The baseline selection window is intentionally fixed at 30 minutes and does not inherit `network_path.collector.pathtest_interval`. It controls selection only, not path-test lifetime: a newly selected path runs immediately and then at the normal `pathtest_interval` until normal TTL expiry. Reselecting a live path refreshes its TTL without resetting its existing cadence, and paths may therefore continue running beyond the window in which they were selected.

signal.title: feat(otel-metrics): share SDK trace stats mapping
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds a transport-neutral `sdktracestats` package under `opentelemetry-mapping-go`. `BuildSDKTraceStatsPayload` owns SDK metric recognition, field mapping, validation, normalized tags, time windows, per-datapoint error isolation, and lossless sparse-histogram construction. The caller supplies envelope metadata such as source and hostname. The package returns shared APM-stats fields without depending on the Agent or dd-source protobuf types. ### Motivation The Agent and public OTLP metrics intake need to convert `traces.span.sdk.metrics.duration` into the same APM trace-stats contract. Keeping two mappings would let tags, status handling, histogram validation, and operation naming drift. This PR makes one mapping implementation the source of truth while leaving transport adapters and delivery local to each consumer. ### Stack and shipping order 1. This PR merges first as the shared code dependency. 2. [ddoghq/dd-source#56526](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/56526) and [DataDog/datadog-agent#53167](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53167) then consume it and can be reviewed in parallel. 3. [ddoghq/dd-go#8800](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-go/pull/8800) can merge independently, but it must deploy before #53167 rolls out. The dd-source rollout does not depend on dd-go. ### Scope - Delta histograms only; the mapping keeps no cumulative-to-delta state. - Invalid datapoints are skipped without discarding valid datapoints in the same metric. - Exact explicit histogram data is preserved in sparse-sketch fields. - No protobuf, HTTP, routing, or deployment behavior is introduced here. ### Validation - `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/opentelemetry-mapping-go/otlp/metrics/...` - `bazel test //pkg/opentelemetry-mapping-go/otlp/metrics/sdktracestats:sdktracestats_test` Both suites pass. Contract coverage includes field mapping, tag normalization, explicit histograms, invalid-datapoint isolation, temporality filtering, fallback windows, and large sparse-bin counts. ### Review focus - Shared field and tag semantics. - Validation/error-isolation behavior. - The boundary between shared mapping logic and consumer-owned transport code.

signal.title: [ABLD-485] Use per-test bazel targets for //pkg/fleet/...
signal.text: **What this does** - Adds `# gazelle:go_test file` to applicable packages under //pkg/fleet/. This let's us get a little more parallelism and lets distinct tests fail independently. **Why** All the reasons in https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/ABLD-485 **Notes** There are a few cases which need explicit handling for test utilities. This happens when the utility methods are helpers for the test, but are named _test.go, as if they are a test. For those, we need to exclude the file from gazelle and then explicitly add it to the test it helps.

Check the [Dependency Dashboard](../issues/33469) for more information. --- ### dd-trace-go: Improper parsing of W3C baggage headers may lead to DoS [CVE-2026-50274](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-50274) / [GHSA-74j5-xf3v-crq8](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-74j5-xf3v-crq8) <details> <summary>More information</summary> #### Details ##### Impact Datadog tracing libraries that implement W3C baggage propagation parse incoming baggage HTTP headers without enforcing item-count or byte-size limits on the extract path. The DD_TRACE_BAGGAGE_MAX_ITEMS (default 64) and DD_TRACE_BAGGAGE_MAX_BYTES (default 8192) limits were applied only to baggage injection, not extraction. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can send a request whose baggage header contains an arbitrarily large number of comma-separated key-value pairs (or a single very large value). The tracer allocates a hash-map entry for each pair on every request, causing unbounded CPU and memory consumption and enabling a remote Denial of Service against any HTTP service that has the baggage propagation style enabled. The baggage propagation style is enabled by default in most affected tracers, so any internet-facing service that has been instrumented with an affected tracer version is exposed unless the propagation style has been explicitly narrowed. ##### Patches This is resolved in version 2.8.1 and later of the `dd-trace-go` library. ##### Workarounds If users cannot upgrade immediately: 1. Disable `baggage` extraction by removing `baggage` from `DD_TRACE_PROPAGATION_STYLE` (or `DD_TRACE_PROPAGATION_STYLE_EXTRACT` if set independently). 2. OTel process context v2 (OTLP proto format) is supported ([#​4478](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4478)), and the `parentbased_always_on` sampler works in OTLP mode ([#​4567](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4567)). **Large Language Model (LLM) Observability.** Prompt tracking is now available for LLMObs spans ([#​4608](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4608)). Experiment scope propagates from APM baggage into spans automatically ([#​4651](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4651)). **Profiler.** An experimental goroutine leak profile is available as opt-in ([#​4420](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4420)). The goroutine wait profile type has been removed — this is a breaking change for anyone using it explicitly ([#​4589](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4589)). **HTTP and tracing.** A new environment variable `DD_TRACE_HTTP_URL_QUERY_STRING_ALLOWLIST` lets you whitelist query string parameters to keep unredacted ([#​4562](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4562)). A new `tracer.StartSpanFromPropagatedContext` API simplifies span creation from propagated contexts ([#​4492](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4492)). AWS EventBridge max payload size is bumped to 1 MB ([#​4458](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4458)). Envoy Service Extensions integration gains Unix Domain Socket (UDS) support ([#​4463](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4463)). **OpenFeature.** Flag evaluation metrics now emit via OTel Metrics ([#​4489](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4489)), with allocation key tagging ([#​4515](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4515)) and Remote Configuration (RC) integration via `FFE_FLAGS` subscription at tracer startup ([#​4495](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4495)). **Bug fixes.** gorm now respects `DD_TRACE_REMOVE_INTEGRATION_SERVICE_NAMES_ENABLED` ([#​4618](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4618)). Redis and Valkey pipeline commands are joined with newlines, fixing agent obfuscation ([#​4593](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4593)). A race condition in HTTP client trace timings is resolved ([#​4591](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4591)). AppSec block responses now include a correct `Content-Length` header ([#​4496](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4496)), and spurious Remote Configuration errors are silenced when RC is disabled ([#​4612](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4612)). `ContextWithSpan` no longer panics on nil context ([#​4313](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4313)). The OTel bridge preserves keep/drop sampling decisions for unsampled spans ([#​4631](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4631)). User-provided DogStatsD addresses now correctly take priority over defaults ([#​4575](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4575)). **Performance.** Trace ID hex encoding is cached ([#​4481](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4481)), the span metadata map is preallocated ([#​4541](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4541)), and locking is removed from both sampling priority access ([#​4546](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4546)) and the internal logger ([#​4547](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4547)) — reducing allocations and contention on hot paths. **CI Visibility.** Bazel offline cache and payload-file modes are supported ([#​4503](https://redirect.github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/pull/4503)). signal.title: [ABLD-461] [ABLD-528] Switch some of pkg/ network and ebpf to select() rather than relying only on tags.
signal.text: [ABLD-461] Switch some of pkg/ network and ebpf to select() rather than relying only on tags. ### What does this PR do? - remove `target_compatible_with = [linux]` on //pkg/epbf. This means a lot of test targets which were silently skipped on other platforms now try to build. - Switch some network and bpf code to hand build select() clauses. - This allows us to make the dependencies match what is actually needed based on the sources which get complied for each tag. - it makes it explicit that ebpf is only used on linux - converts //pkg/network/... to dd_agent_go_test because now that we are trying those tests, we actually need the gotags. - The important outcome: This allows agent to build for macos!!! ### Motivation This unblocks building the agent on all platforms which is a high priority goal, as that unblocks the rest of Q3 work on packaging and security. The alternative is to find and remove every target_compatible_with=linux setting on a transitive dependent of //cmd/agent:agent. To do that - we would have to change every test which might depend on this from go_test to dd_agent_go_test - and probably figure out which ones need explicit linux_bpf tags added, but this adds a new config, wasting CI time - and it is less efficient than just having a smaller build graph. ### Describe how you validated your changes Build and run it on macos. ``` $ bazel run //cmd/agent:agent -- version ... Target //cmd/agent:agent up-to-date: bazel-bin/cmd/agent/agent_/agent INFO: Elapsed time: 7.941s, Critical Path: 7.17s INFO: Running command line: bazel-bin/cmd/agent/agent_/agent <args omitted> Agent 7.83.0-localbuild - Commit: dev - Serialization version: v5.0.205 - Go version: go1.26.5 ``` ### Additional Notes We should remove `--skip_incompatible_explicit_targets` from the global bazelrc. It allowed us to accumulate tech debt by making things that *appeared* to be sound but were silently just not building. Now that we are at the end of the migration, we need to surface the unfinished work. signal.title: fix(devcontainer): don't remap UID on macOS
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Stops the dev container from realigning its `dd` user to the host UID on macOS. `tasks/devcontainer.py` now passes `HOST_UID`/`HOST_GID` **only on Linux**, and sets `updateRemoteUserUID: false`. ### Motivation On macOS the Docker VM's file sharing (virtiofs on Colima/OrbStack, gRPC-FUSE/virtiofs on Docker Desktop) already maps container writes back to the host user regardless of the container UID, so the realignment is unnecessary. Worse, the dev-env image entrypoint's `usermod -u dd` races the dev container CLI's `docker exec -u dd` (onCreateCommand) and aborts the container: ``` usermod: user dd is currently used by process N -> exit 137 ``` Docker Desktop happened to win that race; Colima's `docker exec` timing loses it, so startup fails reliably there — which matters now that engineering is migrating off Docker Desktop to Colima. On native-Linux hosts the IDs are still passed, since bind mounts there preserve the host UID and the realignment is genuinely required. ### Describe how you validated your changes Full `dda inv devcontainer.start` (`devcontainer up` → entrypoint + `install-tools` + `deps`, 191 modules) → `{"outcome":"success"}` on macOS (Apple Silicon) / Colima `vz`+`virtiofs`. ### ⚠️ Also required for macOS: the dev-env image fix This PR is independently correct, but macOS/Colima startup hits a **second, independent** crash: the image entrypoint's `chown -R` of the home dir dies on a unix socket in a bind-mounted `~/.ssh` over virtiofs. That is fixed in **DataDog/datadog-agent-buildimages#1292**, which requires the `datadog/agent-dev-env-linux` image to be **rebuilt and rolled out**. Both this PR and that image bump are needed for macOS to be fully green. ### Possible Drawbacks / Trade-offs None on Linux (behavior unchanged). On macOS/Windows the image-side UID realignment no longer runs, which is the intended fix. ### Release note Dev-tooling change under `tasks/`, no user-facing impact — `changelog/no-changelog`.

signal.title: Skip full git clones on Windows package jobs
signal.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Stop Windows MSI/zip package jobs from doing a full git clone (`GIT_DEPTH: 0`). They only needed history so `get_version()` could run `git describe --tags` inside the build container, which has no AWS credentials. Instead, download `agent-version.cache` on the runner host (after `assume-role`) and fail the job if that copy fails. The file is mounted into the container and xcopied into the buildroot, so `get_version()` reads the cache and never calls `git describe`. ### Motivation Full clones of this repo are expensive. These jobs can use the pipeline-default shallow clone once versioning comes from `setup_agent_version`'s S3 cache. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Confirmed `go_deps` already `needs: setup_agent_version`, so the cache object exists before package jobs start. - Confirmed the host `before_script` `assume-role` still runs (this change is in `script`, so it is not overwritten). - S3 copy uses the same `Invoke-Expression` + `$lastExitCode` pattern as `.upload_sbom_artifacts_windows`, because PowerShell 5 does not fail the job on a native `aws.exe` error. ### Additional Notes CI-only; no release note. Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

signal.title: feat(softinv): report the OS and OEM kernel-mode drivers
signal.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Extends the software inventory beyond installed applications with two new software types, `os` and `driver`: | Platform | Type | Source | |---|---|---| | Windows | `driver` | `Win32_SystemDriver`, plus `Win32_PnPSignedDriver` joined against `Win32_PnPEntity` | | Windows | `os` | `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion` | | macOS | `os` | `/System/Library/CoreServices/SystemVersion.plist` | **Operating system.** One entry whose version advances, rather than one entry per update. An update is an event, not an installed item whose version moves, so it would produce a permanently static entry — and the host SBOM already carries installed KBs. Name and product code are constant, because the backend keys an item on name + product code with the version excluded; anything version-derived in either field would make an upgrade read as remove + install. The version carries the full patch level: `10.0.26100.4652` on Windows including the UBR, `15.6 (24G84)` on macOS including the build that supplemental updates and RSRs advance. **Drivers.** Only OEM and third-party drivers are reported; the drivers that ship with Windows are excluded. Two sources, because each sees what the other cannot. `Win32_SystemDriver` covers drivers registered as kernel services, including software-only ones — EDR minifilters, network and DLP filters — that have no PnP device node. The class carries no version or vendor, so both come from the version resource of the image path; only the numeric `VS_FIXEDFILEINFO` version is accepted, since the `FileVersion` string is routinely decorated or comma-separated. Image paths are normalized (`\??\`, `\SystemRoot\`, `%SystemRoot%`, relative) and MUI display names (`@<dll>,-<id>`) resolved with `SHLoadIndirectString`. Filtered on the binary's `CompanyName`, the only vendor signal the class offers; an absent `CompanyName` is kept, since an unattributed kernel driver is worth seeing. Identity is the service name, which Windows guarantees unique. `Win32_PnPSignedDriver` covers packages bound to a device that register no kernel service of their own, which the first source cannot see. Selected by the INF being published as `oemNN.inf` — `Manufacturer` is not used, because Microsoft's inbox INFs report generic strings such as `(Standard system devices)` and Windows also ships inbox INFs authored by hardware vendors, so filtering on it would keep hundreds of inbox drivers. One `Win32_PnPEntity` query is joined in memory to skip devices that already have a service; a query per device would spend the entire time budget on the join. Identity is the device name, the field the class offers that survives a driver update. Known limitations: UMDF user-mode drivers register no kernel service, and a driver whose service entry is created, loaded, then deleted is invisible. This is an inventory of registered drivers, not of code currently in the kernel. **Deadline.** Each collector is bounded at 90s in the shared snapshot runner. A timeout is fatal, because a timed-out enumeration is an unknown state and a missing row reads downstream as a removal; zero rows is still a valid result. A hung native call cannot be cancelled — the WMI library takes no context — so a collector that misses its deadline is not started again until it returns. ### Motivation The inventory only covered installed applications, leaving OS patch level and kernel drivers invisible — two of the most useful signals for fleet visibility and compliance. The deadline is a prerequisite rather than a nicety: these sources can block, and a single slow `Collect()` previously stalled the whole snapshot with no upper bound. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Windows unit tests run and pass in CI (`tests_windows-x64`); macOS unit tests pass locally; `bazel test //pkg/inventory/software:software_test` passes. - `dda inv linter.go` clean, and clean again under `GOOS=windows`, which type-checks the Windows-tagged files and their tests. - Coverage: deadline and in-flight behaviour, both driver filters, the PnP/service join including case mismatch and devices missing from `Win32_PnPEntity`, path normalization and MUI resolution, the numeric-version requirement, identity stability across a version bump for both driver sources, and entry-ID uniqueness once the new families merge with application entries. - Real-host integration tests compare collected drivers against the `Services` registry key, assert nothing Microsoft-published survives the service filter, and log the OEM/inbox split per source; the macOS one asserts the running version against `sw_vers -productVersion`. - Driver payloads from a real Windows host were inspected end to end. That caught two drivers reporting an unresolved MUI reference as their name, fixed in 2741b66. ### Additional Notes - A fatal error from any single collector still drops the whole snapshot (existing behaviour). - PnP-sourced entries carry no `install_paths`, because `Win32_PnPSignedDriver` names no binary. - Enable with `software_inventory.enabled: true`, which drives both the system-probe module and the core agent component. No status or flare changes were needed, since `populateStatus` already groups by `Source`. - Worst-case snapshot duration is bounded per collector, not globally, so it scales with collector count. A snapshot-wide ceiling would be a separate change.

signal.title: [ACTP] [PAR split deployment] shut down idle private action executor
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds a self-termination watchdog to the on-demand Go executor. Dispatch activity resets the idle timer; health checks do not, and active actions suppress idle shutdown. The watchdog uses three times `private_action_runner.idle_timeout_seconds` (60 seconds by default) so `par-control` remains the primary owner of idle shutdown. It applies only to executor mode; the monolithic runner is unchanged. ### Validation - `bazel test //pkg/privateactionrunner/executor:executor_test` - `bazel test //comp/privateactionrunner/impl:impl_test` - `bazel test //cmd/privateactionrunner/subcommands/runexecutor:runexecutor_test` _Stack 1 of 9; followed by #54589._

signal.title: [SVLS-9526] Prototype: serverless-init inventory payload + 9-platform POC deploy scripts
signal.text: ## What this is A **prototype branch** containing the full stack of changes for SVLS-9526 in a single PR. Intended for review and discussion — these changes will be broken into the stacked PRs below before merge. ## Stacked PRs (final form) | PR | Branch | Contents | |---|---|---| | #54537 | `svls-9526/force-collect` | `ForceCollect()` — send inventory payload on every cold start | | #54538 | `svls-9526/diagnostic-v2` | `inventories_first_run_delay` config key + diagnostic enhancements | | #54543 | `svls-9526/serverless-agent-table` | `cmd/serverless-init/inventory`: `serverless_*` fields in inventoryagent payload | ## What's in this PR **Agent changes (will land via the stacked PRs above):** - `ForceCollect()` added to `inventoryagent.Component` — fires before `modeConf.Runner()` so the inventory payload is sent before the container can scale to zero - `inventories_first_run_delay` config key to control startup delay - New `cmd/serverless-init/inventory` package: populates `serverless_*` fields (cloud provider, workload type, origin, resource name, deployment model, runtime, agent commit, DD config) into the inventoryagent payload - Enhanced startup diagnostics (`DD_SERVERLESS_DIAGNOSTIC_INFO=true`) including UUID, CCRID, and inventory pipeline config **POC deploy scripts (`scripts/serverless-deploy/`, not intended to merge to main):** - Deploys 9 test services across GCP (Cloud Run Service/Job/Function) and Azure (Container App, Web App Containers, Web App SITECONTAINERS, Web App Linux Code) - `demo.sh` — one-command end-to-end runner: build → deploy all 9 → trigger cold starts → collect logs → print REDAPL SQL query ## How to run the POC ```bash export GCP_PROJECT=datadog-serverless-gcp-demo export AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID=<sub-id> export DD_API_KEY=$(vault kv get -field=api_key kv/dd/api_keys/dddev) export IMAGE_TAG=1.10.2-poc-$(date +%Y%m%d) cd scripts/serverless-deploy ./demo.sh ``` ###dd-auth command equivalent: `export DD_API_KEY=$(dd-auth vault kv get -field=api_key kv/dd/api_keys/dddev)` Or if it's wrapping the whole script: `dd-auth ./demo.sh ` Then paste the generated SQL into **go/redapl → Queries → SQL** to see the agents in `datadog_agent`. ## Key findings from 9-platform testing | Platform | UUID behaviour | `datadog_agent` rows | |---|---|---| | GCP Cloud Run | New UUID per cold start | `ForceCollect()` required — container scales to zero before 60s delay | | Azure Container App | Stable UUID per replica | Upserts same row reliably | | Azure Web App | DMI UUID from underlying VM | Apps on same App Service Plan share UUID → need CCRID-based PK | This motivates `serverless_init_agent` (SVLS-9604): a separate REDAPL table keyed by `resource_id` (CCRID) instead of Agent UUID. ## Not in scope for merge - `scripts/serverless-deploy/` — test infrastructure only, not shipped in the agent - `scripts/serverless-deploy/diagnostic-results-*.txt` — personal test output

signal.title: [DO NOT MERGE] One-off e2e run with ADP enabled by default
signal.text: ## Summary Temporarily flips \`data_plane.enabled\` from \`false\` to \`true\` in the agent's compiled-in config default so that every e2e test in the full suite runs against ADP without requiring per-test changes or test duplication. The change is throwaway — close without merging once the CI run completes. This is the same config knob used by the AMP ADP test helpers (DADP-72, see [Slack thread](https://dd.slack.com/archives/C070PQKLLP5/p1783453441368899)). ## How to kick off the full e2e suite Trigger a new pipeline on this branch and set the CI variable: \`\`\` RUN_E2E_TESTS=on \`\`\` That variable hits the \`if_run_all_e2e_tests\` rule in \`.gitlab-ci.yml\` and flips all e2e jobs from manual to \`on_success\`. ## CI findings (ADP 1.5.1, branch jszwedko/run-ci-adp-enabled) ### Fixed in this PR - **Windows MSI \`status_command_infos\`**: All MSI test variants fail because \`agent_behaviour.go\` asserts the status output contains "DogStatsD". When ADP handles DSD, the \`DogStatsD\` status section is absent (the \`EnabledInternal()\` guard prevents registering the status provider). Fixed by accepting either "DogStatsD" or "Dogstatsd Metric Sample" (always present in the Aggregator section). ### Known pre-existing failures (ADP limitations, tracked in Saluki) - **\`TestReplayWithTagEnrichment\`** — ADP doesn't enrich replayed DSD packets with current tagger state. Tracked in Saluki. ### New failures requiring Saluki fixes - **Container DSD tests (ECS \`TestDogtstatsdUDP\`, \`TestDogtstatsdUDS\`; Kind \`dogstatsd-uds\` pods)**: In container environments (ECS, K8s/Kind), fakeintake is configured as \`DD_ADDITIONAL_ENDPOINTS\` rather than \`dd_url\`. ADP doesn't appear to forward DogStatsD metrics to \`additional_endpoints\`, so no metrics arrive at fakeintake. In VM tests where fakeintake IS \`dd_url\` (primary endpoint), DSD forwarding works. This points to an \`additional_endpoints\` forwarding gap in ADP. - The Kind \`dogstatsd-uds\` pods fail to become Ready — the workload pods mount \`/var/run/datadog/dsd.socket\` as a HostPath volume (type \`Socket\`). With ADP enabled, the core agent's DSD server doesn't start (so no socket is created); ADP must create it but apparently doesn't complete socket setup in time or at the expected path. - Root cause: ADP \`additional_endpoints\` forwarding — active Saluki config migration work (issues #2312–#2316) may be the upstream cause. ### Other failures under investigation - **Anomaly detection tests** — under investigation, may be ADP-independent - **GPU tests** — under investigation ## Test plan - No new tests. The goal is to observe which existing e2e tests break when ADP is the default. - \`new-e2e-amp-adp\` (existing) runs the AMP suite filtered to \`--run "ADP"\` tests; this PR covers the rest. **DO NOT MERGE** — this default flip must not land on \`main\`.

signal.title: [TEEP-4881] feat(logs): add metric for messages discarded during file rotation
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds observability for messages discarded during file rotation when `close_timeout` expires: - New `logs.messages_discarded_context_cancelled` telemetry metric - New `MessagesDiscarded` expvar counter - Warning log when messages are discarded with guidance to increase `DD_LOGS_CONFIG_CLOSE_TIMEOUT` ### Motivation In `pkg/logs/tailers/file/tailer.go:424-428`, when the forward context is cancelled (e.g., during rotation timeout), in-flight messages are silently discarded with no telemetry. Users cannot distinguish between "logs were read but discarded" and "logs were never read." This makes it difficult for users with slow pipelines to tune `close_timeout` appropriately since they have no visibility into whether messages are being lost. ### Describe how you validated your changes 1. **Unit test**: Added `TestMessagesDiscardedMetric` that verifies the metric is incremented when messages are discarded due to context cancellation 2. **Manual testing**: Built a debug agent with temporary logging at the discard code path, deployed to EC2, and confirmed the discard triggers during file rotation with a blocked pipeline 3. **Existing tests**: All existing tests in `pkg/logs/metrics` and `pkg/logs/tailers/file` pass ### Additional Notes - This is a low-risk observability enhancement - no changes to existing behavior - The metric name `messages_discarded_context_cancelled` clearly indicates the cause - The warning log includes the `close_timeout` value and suggests increasing `DD_LOGS_CONFIG_CLOSE_TIMEOUT`

signal.title: [PROF-13750] Handle proxy/FIPS/custom URLs in host-profiler converter endpoint inference
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Fixes endpoint inference in the host-profiler converter when `apm_config.profiling_dd_url` or `profiling_additional_endpoints` points to a proxy, FIPS localhost, or other non-Datadog URL. After #46356, `ExtractSiteFromURL` returns empty for any hostname not in the known Datadog domain list. In `newConfigManager` this caused those endpoints to be skipped entirely, leaving inferred OTLP exporters and symbol endpoints empty and stopping profile/symbol delivery. **Changes in `converter_with_agent.go`:** 1. `newConfigManager`: preserve endpoints with empty site when a valid URL is present (previously skipped) 2. `inferOtlpHTTPConfig`: when site is empty, build profiles endpoint as URL + path using `extractBaseURL`; skip metrics with warning 3. `inferHostProfilerEndpointConfig`: when site is empty, skip symbol endpoint inference with warning; disable symbol uploader when no Datadog endpoints available 4. FIPS localhost URLs follow the same proxy path (Info log, not Warn) ### Motivation Users with proxy or FIPS configurations get broken profile/symbol delivery because `ExtractSiteFromURL` returns empty for non-Datadog hostnames, and the converter skips those endpoints entirely. ### Describe how you validated your changes - 3 new golden-file test cases in `TestConverterWithAgentProxyURL`: `proxy_profiling_dd_url`, `fips_localhost_url`, `proxy_additional_endpoint` - Full converter test suite passes with no regressions - Existing Datadog URL tests (`TestConverterWithAgent`, `TestConverterWithAgentDCSite`) still pass ### Additional Notes - **Draft**: Deferring actual implementation until the host-profiler moves from a converter to a confmap provider with a dedicated `datadog.yaml` key for profiler config. This PR serves as a reference implementation. - Jira: PROF-13750 - Depends on: #46356
